title: Setting up and restoring a Blockstream Jade
plain:
Blockstream Jade is a hardware wallet: a small gadget that keeps your bitcoin secrets offline.

Setup means two things. First, the device creates or receives a recovery phrase — a list of 12 or 24 ordinary words that acts like a master password. Jade turns those words into your private keys — the secret numbers needed to spend bitcoin. Second, you protect the phrase with a PIN — a short number code you type to unlock Jade.

1. Turn Jade on by plugging it in or holding the power button. If it is not plugged in, charge it first.

2. Choose Set Up Jade. Most people should pick Begin Setup. Advanced Setup lets you choose the phrase length, make a SeedQR (a square QR barcode that holds your words), or add a BIP39 passphrase (an extra secret password on top of your words).

3. Choose your method. Create New Wallet makes a brand-new recovery phrase. Restore Wallet takes words you already have — from an earlier Jade, another hardware wallet brand (Ledger, Trezor, or Coldcard), or a phone or computer app. You pick 12 or 24 words, or scan a QR code, then type them on Jade's keyboard.

4. Write the words on paper and keep them offline — never photograph them or store them online. Jade checks your copy by asking you to pick the correct word.

5. Connect Jade to a companion app (an app on your phone or computer) using USB, Bluetooth, or QR codes, then set your PIN. The phrase is not stored inside Jade until the PIN is set.

The PIN matters because Jade keeps your phrase scrambled (encrypted), helped by a blind oracle — an outside service that helps unlock the device but cannot read your secrets. A locked Jade resists thieves pulling out its keys.

Words made on a phone or computer keep their old risk even on Jade: payments get approved on the gadget, but the words are no safer. For full cold storage (keys kept only offline), create a new wallet and send your bitcoin to it.

Tip: a fresh Jade can run with nothing saved — you retype your words each time.
technical:
Setting up a Blockstream Jade consists of saving a recovery phrase to the device and protecting it behind a PIN; the recovery phrase derives the private keys required for spending. Jade's security model keeps the phrase encrypted on the device in cooperation with a blind oracle, protecting a locked Jade from physical key extraction, and decryption requires Jade to communicate with a companion device. An uninitialized Jade can alternatively be used as a stateless signing device that stores no wallet information and requires manual recovery phrase entry each session.

Setup flow: (1) power on via USB or the power button, ensuring the battery is charged if running without USB; (2) select Set Up Jade and a Setup Type — Begin Setup (recommended for most users) or Advanced Setup (choose recovery phrase length, export as SeedQR, add a BIP39 passphrase); (3) select a Setup Method — Create New Wallet (generates a new recovery phrase for an unused wallet) or Restore Wallet (imports an existing phrase from a previous Jade, Ledger, Trezor, Coldcard, or software wallet); (4) write the phrase down offline — never photograph it or store it online — and verify the backup by selecting the correct word when prompted; (5) connect to a companion app via USB, Bluetooth, or QR; the recovery phrase is not saved to Jade until PIN setup completes.

Restore flow: power on, select Set up jade, choose Restore Wallet, choose a 12- or 24-word phrase length or recover via QR scan, enter the phrase using Jade's keyboard, then connect to a compatible companion app.

Source caveat: a phrase originally created on a phone or computer app gains hardware signing when restored on Jade, but the security of the phrase itself is unchanged; for full cold storage, create a new wallet and send funds to it.

warnings: Never share your recovery phrase — it grants access to your wallet.
Never enter your recovery phrase on another device except in a genuine emergency.
Do not photograph your recovery phrase or store it online — write it on paper and keep it offline.
Restoring a phrase that was created on a phone or computer app does not make it cold storage; for full cold storage, create a new wallet on Jade and send funds to it.
The recovery phrase is not saved to Jade until PIN setup is complete — finish all setup steps before relying on the device.

notes_for_reviewer: Combined from two Blockstream help pages — re-verify both URLs before publishing, as Blockstream reorganizes its help center. Points to check: (1) The plain-text gloss of the blind oracle ('an outside service that helps unlock the device but cannot read your secrets') is inferred from the term 'blind' and Jade's documented design; the source only says the phrase is encrypted 'in cooperation with a blind oracle' and that decryption requires a companion device — confirm the gloss against Blockstream's security documentation. (2) The source never labels the recovery phrase itself as BIP39 (only the optional passphrase is called a 'BIP39 passphrase'), so neither version asserts that. (3) The Set up page does not enumerate which phrase lengths Advanced Setup offers; the 12/24-word options come from the restore page. (4) The anti-extraction property applies only to a locked Jade, i.e., one with a PIN set. (5) 'Never enter it on another device except for emergency situations' is interpreted as meaning any device other than the Jade hardware wallet itself, since the restore flow requires typing the phrase into Jade. (6) SeedQR is used in the source without definition; the plain-text gloss (a QR barcode holding the words) is standard usage. (7) Staleness risk: UI labels (Set Up Jade / Restore Wallet), connection methods (USB, Bluetooth, QR), and QR-scan restore may change with Jade firmware updates — recheck against current firmware. (8) The note about phrases created on phone/computer apps is a security nuance, not a functional limitation; restoring such a phrase works fine.
